children: China's yuan strengthened to a 3-1/2-year high against the dollar on Monday, defying a near-record weak-side gap in the central bank's daily midpoint guidance as demand for the greenback remained subdued.
strengthened to a high of 6.7050 per dollar in early trades, its strongest level since February 2023, before retreating to 6.7125.
The offshore yuan traded at 6.7113 yuan per dollar
Prior to the market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate
at 6.7795 per dollar. That comes in 709 pips weaker than a Reuters' estimate, the largest weak side deviation since a record seen in February this year.

The central bank has been gradually strengthening its daily yuan official guidance, but at levels weaker than market expectations, suggesting it wants to manages the pace of appreciation, traders and analysts said.
The spot yuan is allowed to trade 2% either side of the fixed midpoint each day.

"CNY remains one of the region's most resilient currencies, but its strength is drawing greater official attention, reflected in the widening counter-cyclical factor in daily USD/CNY fixings," said Geoff Yu, senior EMEA market strategist at BNY.
Flow data also showed that positions have moved further into underweight territory as the pace of yuan appreciation slows, he added.

Chinese banks have been lifting dollar deposit rates and buying U.S. Treasuries over the past few months, moves that could help slow gains in the yuan and which come amid a spike in U.S. yields, Reuters reported.

"The labor market rebound raised expectations of a September Fed rate hike, though the upcoming August CPI report will likely determine whether it goes ahead," analysts at Orient Securities said in a note.
